how_to_read_the_controls: permuted must collapse to chance; if PCA-8 or n=100 match the full head, the signal needs neither dimensions nor examples and is a key being copied, not a readout. v1 scored 100% held out, PASSED its permutation control, and survived both of those -- which is how the label-in-the-prompt was found. All three are printed, always.
the_bar: problems solved and cost on a paired run. Head accuracy is NOT the bar: the arm that localised better and solved half as many would have passed a localisation bar twice, on two different task sets (理.

READING.headline: THE FIRST PROBE IN THIS PROGRAMME THAT BEATS THE AGENT AND SURVIVES ALL THREE CONTROLS.
READING.the_numbers: layer 18: head 56.0% · agent 33.3% · chance 20.4%, on 75 held-out decisions (the last 25% of tasks, no task shared with training). Layer 27: 54.7%.

why_the_controls_matter_more_than_the_he.permutation: mean 16.5% (layer 18) and 18.7% (layer 27) -- COLLAPSES to chance. No label fits.
why_the_controls_matter_more_than_the_he.PCA-8: 28.0% against the full head's 56.0%. The signal NEEDS dimensions.
why_the_controls_matter_more_than_the_he.the contrast with v1: v1's head scored 100% held out, PASSED its permutation control, AND survived PCA-8 and n=100 unchanged -- because the label was a six-row lookup on the prompt. Here all three degrade. THAT PATTERN, not the 56%, is what says this is a learned readout of the state rather than a key being copied.

READING.what_it_does_NOT_establish: that G works. The pre-registration (g_v3_prereg.json, committed before this fit) makes head accuracy explicitly NOT the bar. FAIL-transfer -- the head picks better and the wired run solves no more -- is the reading I named as most likely and it is still open. G-trivial and G-trivial' both raised localisation on two task sets and moved episodes by at most one.
READING.next: wire the argmax into the agent at the post-inspect decision and run the four slices against the base (18.7%, SE 2.2, 10.63 actions). Constraint >= 16.5%; objective >= 23.1% at no higher cost, or the same solved at >= 1.0 action cheaper; confirmation on seed 47.
bounds: 75 held-out decisions. 56.0% vs 33.3% is 17 decisions of 75; the SE on a proportion at n=75 is ~5.7 points, so the gap is ~4 SE and the LEVEL is soft.
The head is fit on candidate states from the same 300-task generator; it has never seen seed 47.

Held out BY TASK (the last 75), not randomly -- so if the generator drifts across its own sequence, that would show here as a train/test difference. It does not appear to: chance is 20.4% on both halves.
